title: Engine: a newer version is offered once, and Settings shows every version
covers: Engine start-up offer and the Engine settings page
context: At start Archipelia offers a newer Archipelago release once. Release notes opens the page and keeps the dialog open. Not now leaves the choice to Engine. There the row Change the engine sits directly under the Archipelago and Python pickers, and installing Archipelago 0.6.6 does not fail at Pack the official worlds.
changed: views/EngineSettings: Versions rows, tags New version, Up to date and Not checked, Installed engines with Active and Last good
hooks/engine-startup: the offer dialog Archipelago X is out

setup.label: engine
setup.text: A ready engine. Step 3 makes it older than the newest stable release, so the offer can appear. The test First run leaves a ready engine.

setup.label: network
setup.text: Needed. The release list and an older version (about 90 MB).

setup.label: data
setup.text: The .user-data\Data folder inside the bundle-4 worktree (X:\archipelia\.worktrees\bundle-4\.user-data\Data).

steps: Launch with the command of this tes If the welcome tour opens, press Under App press In Versions the rows run Archipelago version, Python version, Change the engine, Dependencies, Version list, Look for a new version at s
Change the engine is in view with no scrolling.

In the Archipelago version picker choose the release just below the newest (0.6.6 when the newest is 0.6.7). In Change the engine press Install and switch (or Switch). Every step passes, including Pack the official worlds. Wait for Ready.

Turn on Look for a new version at start. Close Archipelia completely and launch it again. A dialog titled Archipelago X is out opens (X is the newest version) with the buttons Upgrade, Not now and Release notes.

Press Release notes. Your browser opens the release page and the dialog stays open. Press Not now. The dialog closes and nothing is installed. Close and launch again: the offer does not come back for that version.
Open Engine. The rows Archipelago version and Python version each carry the tag New version. Open the Python version picker: a Python 3.13 or newer entry is greyed out with a short reason.
Press Check now on the Version list row. Its line reads Checked followed by a time.
In Installed engines each row shows Archipelago and the version, a line with Python, size, built date and sessions, and the tag Active. The engine used before the last switch has the tag Last good.
Choose the newest release and press Install and switch (or Switch). The tag changes to Up to date. Turn Look for a new version at start off, leave the page and come back. It stays off.
pass: Change the engine sits right under the two pickers, and the 0.6.6 install passes every step including Pack the official worlds.
The offer appears once for the newer version, Release notes keeps the dialog open, Not now closes it without installing, and it does not return for that version.
Both pickers show New version, then Up to date after you move to the newest. The Python picker greys out builds that do not fit, with a reason.
Installed engines show size, sessions, Active and Last good, and the Look for a new version at start switch keeps its value.
fail: Change the engine is far below the pickers, or the 0.6.6 install stops at Pack the official worlds.
The offer appears again for the same version, or never appears although a newer release exists.
Release notes closes the dialog or opens nothing.
A tag is missing or wrong, an incompatible Python can be picked without a reason, or the switch does not keep its value.
notes: The tag Not checked shows when the release list was never read, for example with the network off. Optional check.
With Look for a new version at start off, the offer is skipped. The first-run dialog still appears when no engine exists.
If the Python list has no 3.13 or newer entry, skip the greyed out check in step 6.
The pickers list any stable version, newer or older. If 0.6.6 is not listed, install the release just below the newest and say which one in your note.
